instructions.task: Read the Craigslist item listing and the buyer-seller negotiation chat. Did the negotiation close with a deal?
instructions.background: The chat is the talk before a formal offer is submitted and accepted outside the chat, so chats often stop right after the two sides converge, sometimes before the last counteroffer is answered in words. Most negotiations that reach a concrete price with a cooperative tone end in a deal.
rules: A deal: a price was offered and the other side accepted it, even informally ('fair enough', 'ok', 'X will work', 'you've got a deal', 'done', 'put in your offer', 'that's a pretty good deal'), even with a side condition such as pickup, delivery or extras.

A deal: the seller goes along with the buyer's price (or names a price close to it) and the chat ends on logistics (pickup, meeting, delivery, 'on my way', 'today will work') or pleasantries, with no refusal.
A deal: the chat ends with a counteroffer that is close to the other side's last offer and nobody has refused; they are converging cooperatively.
No deal: the conversation has only one or two messages in total, even if one of them names a price, says 'I will take X' or 'I'll go 5 lower'.

No deal: for a rental, the monthly rent was never agreed, e.g. the landlord restates the rent without the tenant accepting, or agrees to the tenant's number only as a deposit. A landlord who accepts the tenant's rent on a condition (sign today, longer lease) has agreed: that is a deal.
No deal: the chat ends right after one side's first price offer, before the other side has replied to that offer.
No deal: the seller just repeats the same firm price they already stated, refusing to move, and the buyer has not accepted it.
No deal: the chat never gets to bargaining over a price (only questions about the item, or off-topic), or is empty, one or two lines, or nonsense.
No deal: one side clearly refuses the final price, says they are too far apart, or walks away; or one side says the submitted offer does not match what they can pay.
No deal: both sides have stated firm limits that do not meet (the buyer's stated maximum is well below the seller's stated rock-bottom or lowest price) and nobody gives in.

explicit_agreement.description: Deal: one side made a price offer and the other side accepted it, even informally or with a side condition.
examples: Buyer: I can do 70 / Seller: Okay then you still will have to come pick it up yourself / Buyer: ok
Buyer: Will you sell it to me for $150? / Seller: ...I am letting it go at $175... / Buyer: Fair enough. / Seller: Great doing business with you
Seller: you've got a deal. 28500 and your car for trade in.
Buyer: $40 is good, yea? / Seller: ok, 0 will do. what's your PHONE#?
Buyer: how about we meet halfway and you bring it down $15 / Seller: Yeah I do that put in your offer.
Seller: 2700 is too low... How about 3000? / Buyer: That's a pretty good deal I must say. But I was hoping it came with handcuffs
Buyer: is there any way you could reduce the rent to 1600 a month / Seller: If you can come today and sign your lease with me I will allow you the reduction in rent. [chat ends]

agreed_then_logistics.description: Deal: the price was accepted or not disputed and the chat ends arranging pickup, meeting, delivery, payment, paperwork or the formal offer.
examples: Buyer: I can give you $240 for it... could I swing by and pick it up? / Seller: [describes phone] ...we could meet at a starbucks. What day would be good for you? / Buyer: Today will work, thanks!
Seller: I have someone else interested at $40 but I'll go with you if you can get here in 30 minutes / Buyer: I am on my way! Thanks / Seller: Thank you.
Buyer: Would you be able to do $400 and deliver? / Seller: That sounds very reasonable... Ok submit your final offer, I will fix the ring and deliver

Buyer: Well, that doesn't sound like a bad deal. I think we will submit an offer for it. / Seller: Thanks for your interest, we'll submit the papers to you promptly. [a rental where the tenant accepts the listed rent]

converging_open_end.description: Deal: the chat ends with a counteroffer or conditional reply close to the other side's price, no one refuses, and the tone is cooperative.
examples: Buyer: I think you found a buyer... would $22 do? / Seller: 25 and you got yourself a deal [chat ends]
Buyer: $10000 and you bring it to me / Seller: 10000 and you will come get it yourself [chat ends]
Seller: I think 1300 will work since i need to get it sold / Buyer: Oh, sorry for being rude
Seller: What about $1350? / Buyer: Sounds reasonable, would you be able to deliver it at that price? / Seller: ...I should be able to include shipping.
Buyer: I'd like to offer $9200 for it. / Seller: I am sorry but this is a Lexus... I would of went off $500 but since you have 9200 [chat ends]
Buyer: Would you take $100? / Seller: I can't go quite that low, but I could probably give it to you for 175. [chat ends]
Buyer: $14800 and we have a deal. / Seller: $14900 is my final offer. [chat ends]
Seller: I'll give you 900$ for guts, but that's my best offer. / Buyer: It is a great bike. / Seller: I think it's worth it.

no_price_bargaining.description: No deal: the chat ends before the two sides bargain over a price, e.g. only the listing price is stated and the other side just asks questions about the item.
examples: Seller: I am selling it for 75$ are you interested? / Buyer: Yes. It looks great. I would like to be sure I won't get in any trouble if I am caught with it though. Did you alter the device? [chat ends]

offer_mismatch.description: No deal: one side says the formal offer shows a different price than they agreed or can afford, or refuses it.
examples: Seller: Ok that is fine with me! / Buyer: The offer says 2695 but I can only afford 2200.00

rejected_or_walked_away.description: No deal: one side refused the final price, said they are too far apart, gave up, or left; or both sides stated firm limits that do not meet (buyer's maximum well below seller's rock bottom).
examples: Buyer: That's still too low partner, we're looking at maximum $9000. / Seller: I'm sad to hear that. My rock bottom price is $11,000. If you can see your way to make that great. [chat ends]

criteria.broken_or_off_topic: No deal: the conversation is empty or has only one or two messages in total (even 'I will take 70' or 'Yes, I'll go 5 lower'), nonsense, about a different item, or never negotiates.

rent_not_agreed.description: No deal: a rental where the monthly rent was never agreed by both sides; the landlord restates the rent, or agrees to the tenant's figure only as a deposit, and the tenant never accepts a rent.
examples: Buyer: Would you be willing to take $100 less a month. / Seller: it a real nice appt with a 12 month lease 2200 month with 2200 depost also sound good [chat ends]
Buyer: How about $1600 a month? / Seller: $1600 is fine for a deposit, and we're happy to pick you up for a tour / Buyer: Alright, I think I can come in later today

first_offer_unanswered.description: No deal: the chat ends with the first price offer (or first request for a discount) still unanswered; bargaining never got a reply. If the other side did reply with a counteroffer close to it, this is not the right option.
examples: Buyer: ...the price is a little steep would you like to go down to $20K if I picked this up? [chat ends]
Buyer: my target price is $300. If I picked it up within the next two hours could you agree to that price? [chat ends]
Buyer: I hate to low ball you... but would you consider 60.00 cash? [chat ends]

seller_holds_firm.description: No deal: the seller repeats the same price they already insisted on, without moving toward the buyer, and the buyer never accepts.
examples: Seller: $100 is the least I'll take for both chairs / Buyer: can we do $80. I would have to rent a truck / Seller: 100 plus the rug and I'll deliver [chat ends]
